text.p: 50-Off Stores Inc said on Monday a U.S. Bankruptcy court approved a $15 million debtor-in-possession (DIP) revolving credit facility from a major financial institution.
Funding under the facility was available on Monday, the company said.
50-Off Stores and its significant subsidiaries filed petitions for protection under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code on October 9, the company said.
The debtor-in-possession financing was expected to give management important financial resources needed to put together a reorganization plan, the company said.
Proceeds from the facility would be used to refinance certain debt secured before the petition, and to provide working capital, the company said.
The facility, which matures in 12 months, had a floating rate interest equal to the published rate for 30-day commercial paper issued by major corporations plus three percent per year, 50-Off said.
